podcast.title: Wayne's World Soundtrack (1992) Dominance
podcast.body: The first *Wayne's World* CD from 1992 was noted for being "mostly classic rock." While it also featured contemporary alternative bands like the Red Hot Chili Peppers and Soundgarden, its overall composition leaned heavily towards established rock sounds. "The first Wayne's World CD from 92 is pretty good, although it's mostly classic rock."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Defined by Older Acts in Early 1990s
podcast.body: The term "classic rock" began to be defined in the early 1990s by established acts like the Rolling Stones, Pink Floyd, and Elton John, as hair metal was losing its appeal. This categorization emerged as a way to describe older, enduring rock artists. "It was also dominated by older acts that were defining a new term, classic rock, Rolling Stones, Pink Floyd, Elton John, and so on."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 1: Rock Struggles Again

podcast.title: Definition and Lineage
podcast.body: "Classic rock" is a term used to describe bands such as Van Halen, Aerosmith, The Rolling Stones, and Led Zeppelin. Their musical traditions are deeply rooted in the blues, with spiritual ancestors identified as figures like Robert Johnson and Howlin' Wolf, distinguishing them from genres grounded in punk. "At the other end of the spectrum, Van Halen and Eros Smith and the Rolling Stones and Led Zeppelin are now described as classic rock. Their sonic traditions are grounded in the blues, not punk."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Included in Antichrist Superstar
podcast.body: Elements of Classic Rock were integrated into the musical complexity of Marilyn Manson's "Antichrist Superstar," alongside other diverse genres. "se mete dentro del rock clásico."

srcs.episode: Cómo Marilyn Manson revolucionó el mundo con Antichrist Superstar

podcast.title: Industry Figures at Awards
podcast.body: The UK Classic Rock Awards featured prominent figures from the classic rock world, such as Jimmy Page and Steven Tyler, indicating the genre's significant industry presence and influence. "Jimmy Page was there and Stephen Tyler was there and all these insane giants from the Classic Rock world were there."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Trews: In Their Own Words

podcast.title: Insatiable Market (Mid-1980s)
podcast.body: As rock declined and pop ascended by mid-1984, many rock fans turned to the music of the 1960s and 1970s, creating an "insatiable market for what was now being called classic rock." "Many rock fans turned to the 60s and 70s, creating an insatiable market for what was now being called classic rock."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Alt Rock Chapter: 14

podcast.title: Mainstream Rejection (Late 1980s)
podcast.body: By the late 1980s, classic rock was among the mainstream genres that fans of alternative and non-mainstream music deliberately avoided. This audience sought out unique sounds in indie clubs and record stores, contrasting with the music widely available on Top 40 radio. "You want nothing to do with hair metal or classic rock or new kids on the block or anything on top 40 radio."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Soloing Style Comparison
podcast.body: Classic rock guitar solos were often characterized by a rapid "100 notes a second" style, which was generally not adopted as a core part of alt rock culture. "For years, alt rock guitarists issued classic rock style guitar solos that featured 100 notes a second. That sort of playing was not part of alt rock culture."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Support for New Music
podcast.body: Classic Rock magazine in the UK is noted for its supportive stance towards new music, particularly for bands that fit its promotional mold. This support led to The Trews being nominated for awards and having their albums reviewed and distributed by the magazine. "They, that's a very supportive magazine of like new music just generally."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
